section_summary: This section continues a report on Japan’s economic stabilization program in 1949. It examines falling investment and demand, accumulating stockpiles, strained industries, unemployment, and the effects on household and farm incomes. It closes with proposals for exports, prices, business rationalization, investment, and living standards.

subfiles.title: Report on the effects of Japan’s economic stabilization program
subfiles.about: The report assesses Japan’s 1949 economic slowdown and the effects of stabilization on industry, employment, farms, prices, and living standards.
subfiles.summary: The report links reduced public works and equipment financing to weaker demand, growing inventories and unpaid accounts, and stagnating industrial production. It surveys the effects across major industries and small businesses, then examines wages, unemployment, farm finances, and urban household consumption. Its final sections call for stronger exports and investment, careful changes to subsidies and prices, and broader economic rationalization to support a self-supporting economy.
